name: Birgitz
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village on the Sonnenplateau, perched above the Inntal valley, offering breathtaking views of the Stubaier Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Birgitz is an idyllic municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district of Tyrol, situated at an altitude of approximately 859 meters on a sunny low-mountain terrace southwest of the provincial capital Innsbruck. Home to around 1,520 residents and spanning nearly five square kilometers, the charming village nestles amidst lush green meadows beneath the craggy peaks of the Kalkkögel and Mount Nockspitze (2,404 m). Despite being only ten kilometers away from Innsbruck, Birgitz has retained its authentic rural village character, characterized by historic timber farmsteads and an unhurried alpine lifestyle. The sunny slopes offer commanding panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley towards the jagged limestone wall of the Nordkette range. The municipality belongs to the Innsbruck region.

History

Human habitation in the area dates back to pre-Christian antiquity. Between the 4th and 1st centuries BC, the forested hill of Hohe Birga hosted one of the most prominent fortified hilltop settlements of the Raetian Fritzens-Sanzeno culture in North Tyrol. These terraced alpine structures with sunken ground floors (Casa Raetica) were destroyed by fire around 15 BC during the Roman conquest of the Alps under Emperor Augustus. The settlement was first documented in 1286 under the name Purgitz. A fascinating historical legacy is the solemn Plague Vow of 1727: after surviving devastating epidemics, villagers pledged never to celebrate secular carnival festivities again, making Birgitz the only village in the region without carnival traditions. The Baroque parish church of the Visitation of the Virgin Mary was built between 1727 and 1728 by master builder Gallus Gratl, featuring beautiful ceiling frescoes by Josef Anton Kirchebner.

How to Get There

Motorists reach Birgitz via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Innsbruck-West or Zirl-Ost/Kematen, and continuing along the scenic plateau road L12 via Völs and Götzens in approximately fifteen minutes. Rail travelers arrive at Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, connecting directly with frequent VVT regional bus line 404 to the village square. In winter, dedicated ski buses transport winter sports enthusiasts directly to the nearby Axamer Lizum Olympic ski resort and the Muttereralm cable cars.

Tips

A major cultural attraction is the Hohe Birga archaeological open-air site, an accessible terrain featuring conserved stone foundations of Raetian dwellings along an informative educational trail. In the village center, the Birgitz Raetian Museum showcases remarkable archaeological artifacts including bronze brooches, ceramics, and weaving tools. Hikers enjoy ascending to the rustic Birgitzer Alm pasture at 1,808 meters, offering stunning panoramas of the Stubai Alps and a popular 3.5-kilometer natural toboggan run in winter. Mountain enthusiasts can summit the Nockspitze or Birgitzköpfl. Positioned conveniently between the Axamer Lizum and Muttereralm ski areas, Birgitz serves as an ideal base for outdoor adventures year-round.
